solutionReview.headline: Measure time from $t={{t0}}$ and count periods of {{k}}: $Q(t)={{M}}({{g}})^{(t-{{t0}})/{{k}}}$.
reasoning: The value is {{M}} at $t={{t0}}$, so the exponent must be 0 there: use $t-{{t0}}$. Each {{k}} units is one factor of {{g}}, so divide by {{k}}.
Check: at $t={{t0k}}$ the exponent is $\frac{{{t0k}}-{{t0}}}{{{k}}}=1$, and the value is ${{M}}\cdot {{g}}={{Mg}}$.
solutionReview.commonError: Using $t$ instead of $t-{{t0}}$, which puts the value {{M}} at $t=0$ instead of at $t={{t0}}$.

solutionReview.headline: Two steps multiply by $b^2$; anchor at $x=1$: $f(x)={{M}}({{b}})^{x-1}$.
reasoning: From $x=1$ to $x=3$ the function is multiplied by $b$ twice: $b^2=\frac{{{N}}}{{{M}}}={{b2}}$, so $b={{b}}$.
The value {{M}} is at $x=1$, so the exponent is $x-1$: $f(x)={{M}}({{b}})^{x-1}$. Check: ${{M}}({{b}})^2={{N}}$ at $x=3$.
solutionReview.commonError: Writing ${{M}}({{b}})^x$, which gives {{M}} at $x=0$ instead of at $x=1$.

solutionReview.headline: Factor $\frac{{{factor}}}{100}$ once every 2 years, counted from year {{y0}}.
reasoning: Increasing by {{p}}% multiplies by $\frac{{{factor}}}{100}$: $100\%+{{p}}\%={{factor}}\%$.
The value is {{A}} at $t={{y0}}$ and the factor applies once every 2 years, so the exponent is $\frac{t-{{y0}}}{2}$.
So $V(t)={{A}}\left(\dfrac{{{factor}}}{100}\right)^{(t-{{y0}})/2}$.
solutionReview.commonError: Using $\frac{{{p}}}{100}$ as the factor (that shrinks the value), or counting time from 0 instead of from year {{y0}}.

reasoning: Dividing by {{d}} is multiplying by $\frac{1}{{{d}}}$.
The value is {{M}} at $x=1$ and the factor applies once per increase of 2, so the exponent is $\frac{x-1}{2}$; at $x=3$ it is $\frac{3-1}{2}=1$.
